newsitem.title: USA: General Re sees profit growth at swaps unit.
newsitem.headline: General Re sees profit growth at swaps unit.

text.p: General Re Corp expects revenue and profits at its swaps and derivatives unit to double by 1999, a company executive said.

Tom Kellogg, president and chief operating officer of General Reinsurance Corp, the principal subsidiary of the holding company General Re, said unit General Re Financial Products Corp is developing plans to double revenues and profits by 1999.

Kellogg, speaking at the National Insurance Symposium Conference in San Francisco, said General Reinsurance expects to assume risk at a rate equal to $100 million a year in so-called employment practices liability by the end of 1998.
Kellogg also said pressure has been building on reinsurers because the insurance industry is overcapitalized and retention levels are increasing.
"The effect is demand is down for reinsurance from the large national insurance companies," he told Reuters after his speech.
Kellogg said he was happy with General Reinsurance's 1996 results. In 1996, the General Re group wrote about $6.7 billion in net premiums written.
He said the group ended the year with $1.35 billion in asbestos and environmental reserves.
"And I feel comfortable with that level," he said.
Kellogg said in General Re's two global facultative initiatives the company plans to quickly expand outside the United States.
Asked if reinsurers would move aggressively into the Asian market, Kellogg said, "The numbers are overwhelming and the potential is certainly there."
But, he added, "It will take time."
